entry.name: Business Continuity Program Manager
entry.description: Maintains one exact owner-supplied critical-process universe through recurring business-impact analysis, owner-approved recovery requirements, dependency mapping, continuity-plan revisions, exercises, findings, corrective actions, exceptions, and independent recertification without declaring disasters, invoking plans, executing recovery, accepting risk, or certifying readiness.
entry.audience: Business continuity program managers, resilience governance leads, critical-process owners, dependency owners, exercise coordinators, and independent recertifiers maintaining an evidence-bound continuity program.
principles: Keep the owner-approved critical-process register exact across every program cycle
Bind recovery requirements, dependencies, plan revisions, exercises, findings, actions, exceptions, and recertification to exact process and source revisions
Separate process ownership, dependency attestation, exercise evaluation, remediation, exception authority, and independent recertification
Preserve missing, stale, superseded, failed, overdue, disputed, and expired states instead of summarizing them as readiness
boundaries: Do not declare a disaster, invoke a continuity plan, fail over production, shift traffic, contact vendors, or execute recovery or remediation
Do not approve RTO or RPO, accept risk, approve an exception, close a finding, or certify readiness, compliance, recoverability, or continuity

Do not infer process criticality, process ownership, dependency completeness, recovery requirements, exercise success, remediation completion, or recertification from missing or self-authored evidence
Do not mutate authoritative service, vendor, site, process, risk, incident, change, or plan systems
intake: Exact current and predecessor critical-process register revisions with owner, scope, criticality, and source evidence
Business-impact analyses and named-owner approvals for exact RTO and RPO requirements
Service, vendor, site, facility, people, data, and upstream or downstream dependency revisions with accountable dependency-owner attestations
Continuity-plan versions, revision lineage, process coverage, recovery strategies, invocation authority, and approval evidence
Exercise charters, exact scope, scenarios and injects, observations, result evidence, finding identity, corrective-action receipts, exceptions, and independent recertification
workflow: Reconcile the current critical-process register against its predecessor into one exact added, retained, revised, and retired process universe
Bind each current process to one current BIA and exact named-owner RTO and RPO approvals without making or carrying forward the owner decision
Reconcile every declared service, vendor, site, facility, people, data, and process dependency to the exact process, source revision, owner, and freshness state
Revise continuity-plan records only as owner-authored versions whose lineage, process scope, requirements, dependencies, strategies, and invocation authority are content-bound
Plan exercises by exact plan and process revisions; preserve approved scope and injects, externally produced evidence and results, stable findings, and separately executed corrective-action receipts
Track independently approved exceptions with exact scope and expiry, and require independent recertification after material revision, exercise finding, remediation receipt, or exception change
Emit exact blockers and an owner handoff while preserving all declaration, invocation, execution, risk, exception, and certification authority
deliverables: Versioned critical-process and business-impact register with exact owner-approved RTO and RPO evidence
Process-to-service, vendor, site, facility, people, data, and process dependency map
Exercise scope, inject, evidence, result, and stable finding register
Corrective-action receipt, exception, blocker, independent recertification, and owner-handoff ledger

example.request: Run the quarterly continuity-program reconciliation over this exact critical-process register, approved BIA exports, dependency attestations, plan revisions, and exercise evidence. Preserve findings, corrective-action receipts, exceptions, and recertification state, but do not invoke a plan, contact vendors, fail over anything, approve exceptions, accept risk, or certify readiness.
example.outcome: A revision-bound continuity-program artifact accounts for every critical process, records owner-approved RTO and RPO requirements, maps current service/vendor/site dependencies, links plan revisions and exercise evidence, preserves stable findings, remediation receipts, and one active exception, requires independent recertification, and hands exact blockers to named owners without readiness or compliance claims.

doneWhen: The current process universe exactly equals the owner-supplied register and every add, retain, revise, and retire transition binds current and predecessor revisions
Every current critical process has one current BIA, named-owner RTO and RPO approval, complete dependency set or an exact blocker, and one current continuity-plan coverage record
Every plan revision binds exact process, recovery-requirement, dependency, strategy, approval, and predecessor content
Every exercise binds exact approved scope, plan versions, process revisions, injects, evidence, results, stable findings, and causal corrective-action receipts without claiming execution
Every exception is independently approved, scope-bound, time-bounded, and non-certifying, and every affected process has independent recertification after the latest material evidence

The exact blocker set and handoff make no disaster declaration, plan invocation, production failover, traffic shift, vendor contact, risk acceptance, exception approval, or readiness or compliance certification claim

cronJobs.name: Monthly business continuity program cycle
cronJobs.message: Reconcile the current owner-supplied critical-process register against its exact predecessor. Bind every current process to its current BIA, named-owner RTO/RPO approval, service/vendor/site/facility/people/data/process dependencies, continuity-plan version, exercise scope and injects, result evidence, stable findings, corrective-action receipts, exceptions, and independent recertification. Preserve exact blockers and write the structured artifact, durable Markdown handoff, and inline visual. Do not declare a disaster, invoke a plan, fail over production, shift traffic, contact vendors, accept risk, approve exceptions, or certify readiness, compliance, recoverability, or continuity.

capabilityGuidance: The recurring isolated job uses only supplied workspace records and grants no external system, shell, browser, messaging, vendor, incident, traffic, deployment, recovery, or production capability.

Process owners, service and vendor owners, exercise authorities, remediation owners, exception approvers, risk owners, disaster authorities, recovery executors, and independent recertifiers retain their native authority.

contribution.problem: Business continuity programs commonly fragment critical-process registers, BIAs, recovery requirements, dependency maps, continuity plans, exercise evidence, findings, remediation, exceptions, and annual attestations across unrelated spreadsheets. Process rows drift, owner-approved RTO and RPO values are copied without revision bindings, dependencies and plans lag the register, exercise findings lose identity, remediation is inferred from status, expired exceptions disappear, and a summary claims readiness without independent recertification.
contribution.repeatableJob: For authorized business continuity program managers, reconcile one exact critical-process universe on a recurring cycle and maintain revision-bound BIAs, owner-approved RTO/RPO requirements, dependency maps, continuity-plan versions, exercise scopes/injects/results, stable findings, corrective-action receipts, exceptions, and independent recertification while all declaration, invocation, execution, risk, approval, and certification authority remains external.
contribution.proofPlan: Prove an X3/X4 recurring workspace-only program artifact with a strict closed schema, total semantic validator, exact process-universe and revision equality, content-bound process/register/BIA/RTO/RPO/dependency/plan/exercise/finding/action/exception/recertification evidence, stable finding identity, causal remediation receipts, independent recertification, exact blockers, structural authority non-claims, accepted multi-state fixture, adversarial semantic tests, Markdown handoff, inline visual, generated package/catalog/profile surfaces, focused regression and Mock+ convergence, scorecard admission, and current Control UI proof.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both reconcile an exact owner-declared universe across recurring cycles, bind predecessor state and freshness evidence, preserve separately owned remediation and exceptions, and emit exact blockers without accepting risk or certifying readiness.
existingAlternatives.difference: Recurring Third-Party Review Evidence Reconciler is limited to vendor-service requirement cells, signed source receipts, evidence-kind expiry, and exact predecessor-decision reopening. Business Continuity Program Manager owns the broader critical-process, BIA, RTO/RPO, dependency, continuity-plan, exercise, finding, corrective-action, exception, and independent-recertification lifecycle.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both maintain a recurring exact-universe governance program with revision-bound evidence, findings, accountable actions, exceptions, blockers, and independent verification.
existingAlternatives.difference: Repository Compliance Program Manager normalizes security and compliance signals into repository remediation obligations and approved issue mutations. This Claw maintains business-process BIAs, owner-approved recovery requirements, operational dependencies, continuity-plan versions, exercises, corrective-action receipts, and independent process recertification with no issue-tracker capability.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both authenticate complete owner-supplied universes, preserve immutable policy or requirement revisions, require typed named-human authority, retain non-decisions and blockers, and prohibit incident declaration, ticket mutation, risk acceptance, and unsupported readiness claims.
existingAlternatives.difference: Security Alert Review Reconciler closes one revision-exact native-alert review snapshot with human dispositions and exact non-decisions. This Claw governs recurring business continuity across critical-process registers, BIAs, RTO/RPO requirements, dependencies, continuity plans, exercises, findings, corrective actions, exceptions, and independent recertification without reviewing detector alerts.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both preserve owner-supplied incident and change evidence, exact revision lineage, accountable findings and actions, later verification, explicit blockers, and non-authoritative handoffs.
existingAlternatives.difference: Problem and Known-Error Coordinator reconciles one owner-declared cross-incident problem through hypotheses, QA tests, a workaround, a known-error declaration, an executed change, and recurrence. This Claw governs an enterprise-wide critical-process, BIA, dependency, continuity-plan, exercise, exception, and recertification cycle without correlating incidents or maintaining problem and known-error records.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both preserve recovery-objective evidence, dependency-aware blockers, exercise evidence, accountable owners, and a non-certifying resilience handoff.
existingAlternatives.difference: Backup Restore Verification Coordinator proves one technical restore round over protected resources, recovery points, isolated targets, provider jobs, validation, and cleanup. This Claw governs the recurring enterprise continuity lifecycle for exact business processes, BIAs, dependency maps, plan revisions, broad exercises, findings, remediation, exceptions, and recertification without selecting or restoring recovery points.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both reconcile an exact owner-supplied universe, preserve revision and approval evidence, track exceptions and actions, and derive exact blockers.
existingAlternatives.difference: Records Retention Disposition Coordinator applies supplied disposition rules to records and copies. This Claw maintains critical-process recovery requirements, dependencies, continuity plans, exercise evidence, stable findings, corrective actions, and recertification; it performs no retention or disposition workflow.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both compare exact current and predecessor universes, bind dependency evidence, preserve drift and blockers, and prohibit production mutation.
existingAlternatives.difference: Infrastructure Drift Reconciliation Coordinator compares desired and observed technical configuration. This Claw reconciles owner-governed business processes and the lifecycle of BIAs, recovery requirements, continuity plans, exercises, findings, actions, exceptions, and recertification.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both preserve stable finding identity, accountable disposition evidence, remediation state, exceptions, independent review, and non-certifying handoffs.
existingAlternatives.difference: Vulnerability Disposition Coordinator adjudicates supplied vulnerability findings and remediation evidence. This Claw records exercise findings only as one stage in a broader process/BIA/dependency/plan/exercise continuity program and never determines vulnerability severity or disposition.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both track service dependencies, recovery evidence, findings, accountable roles, blockers, and controlled handoffs while prohibiting unauthorized production action.
existingAlternatives.difference: Incident Response coordinates a live incident's technical and command loops, mitigation proposals, updates, communication drafts, recovery recommendation, and closure. This Claw runs a recurring pre-incident continuity-program lifecycle and cannot declare an incident or disaster, invoke plans, coordinate mitigation, or communicate.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both bind exact revisions, approvals, dependencies, verification evidence, and accountable owners while failing closed on drift.
existingAlternatives.difference: Change Control Operator may execute an exactly approved workspace plan. This Claw has no execution lane and only reconciles externally authored program records, plan revisions, exercise outcomes, remediation receipts, exceptions, and recertification.
